mainTopic: A pinched or slaughtered bird that turns out to be a טריפה: the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the rule of דיו, and each side's source in the פסוקים.
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about a bird offering killed by מליקה (pinching the neck) that then turns out to be a טריפה. Does it make the person who swallows it טמא, like any dead kosher bird? רבי יהודה says yes. רבי מאיר says no. He argues by קל וחומר from an animal that שחיטה protects a טריפה bird, and then says מליקה should work just like שחיטה. רבי יוסי limits him with the rule of דיו: what is learned from an animal cannot go beyond the animal, so only שחיטה helps. The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר could ignore דיו, which the Torah teaches through the story of מרים. It answers that רבי מאיר really learns his view from the פסוק "זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף": whatever makes an animal or bird fit to eat also protects a טריפה from טומאה. רבי יהודה learns his view from the extra word טרפה in ויקרא 17:15, which he reads as including a slaughtered טריפה. רב שיזבי challenges this reading by comparing the פסוק about fat, where the same word only leaves out non-kosher animals. The גמרא defends רבי יהודה with a ברייתא showing he leaves out a non-kosher bird using the word נבלה instead.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the pinched bird that turns out to be a טריפה makes the eater impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that an עולת העוף killed by מליקה and found to be a טריפה still makes a person טמא when he swallows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: it makes the eater impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי יהודה's opinion: a pinched bird offering that turns out to be a טריפה acts like any dead kosher bird and makes the person who swallows it טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the killing does not save a bird that turns out to be a טריפה from the טומאה of a נבלה. As the גמרא shows later (steps 10-11), he holds this even for a טריפה bird that had a proper שחיטה, so מליקה certainly does not help. A נבלת עוף טהור makes the eater טמא in the בית הבליעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes impure. Here it means it makes the person who swallows it טמא.
An animal or bird with a fatal defect. It is forbidden to eat even after a proper killing.
Killing a bird offering by pinching its neck from the back with the כהן's fingernail.
A kosher bird that died without a proper killing. It makes a person טמא only when swallowed.
The throat. This is the place where a dead kosher bird makes a person impure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it renders impure.
phrases.notes: He means the bird makes the person who swallows it טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's side of the dispute about the pinched bird that turned out to be a טריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird offering killed by מליקה and found to be a טריפה makes the one who swallows it טמא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's קל וחומר: slaughter protects a טריפה bird from impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר proves with a קל וחומר from an animal that שחיטה stops a bird that is a טריפה from becoming a טמא נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: this is a קל וחומר. A dead animal makes a person impure by touching and by carrying, and still its slaughter keeps it from impurity even if it is a טריפה. A dead bird does not make a person impure by touching or carrying. So surely its slaughter should keep it from impurity even if it is a טריפה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר begins proving his view that the bird is not טמא. This first stage shows that שחיטה of a bird that is a טריפה prevents its טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלת בהמה has stronger טומאה (it works by touching and by carrying), yet a שחיטה still protects a טריפה animal from it. A נבלת עוף has weaker טומאה (it works only by swallowing). So it is all the more logical that שחיטה protects a טריפה bird. This step only proves the rule for שחיטה; the move to מליקה comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument, from a stricter case to a lighter one.
Touching.
Carrying. You become impure by carrying the item even without touching it.
The carcass of an animal that was not properly slaughtered.
'Isn't it logical?' The words that close a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said: it is an a fortiori argument;
if the carcass of an animal,
which makes impure through touching and through carrying –
its slaughter purifies it, even when it is a tereifa, from its impurity;
the carcass of a bird,
which does not make impure through touching and through carrying –
is it not logical that its slaughter
should purify it, even when it is a tereifa, from its impurity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבי מאיר's argument against רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That שחיטה keeps a bird that is a טריפה from the טומאה of a נבלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from נבלת בהמה, whose stronger טומאה is still prevented by שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר stretches the rule from slaughter to pinching
steps.stepSummary: Using a מה מצינו comparison, רבי מאיר argues that מליקה should also protect a bird that is a טריפה, just as שחיטה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we found that slaughter makes a bird fit to eat and also keeps it from impurity even if it is a טריפה, so too pinching, which makes the bird offering fit to eat, should keep it from impurity even if it is a טריפה!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second stage of רבי מאיר's proof. He moves the rule he just proved for שחיטה over to מליקה, which is the actual case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His comparison works like this: שחיטה makes an ordinary bird fit to eat, and מליקה makes a bird offering fit to eat. If the act that makes it fit to eat also protects a טריפה from טומאה in one case, it should do the same in the other. That is how he reaches his ruling: the pinched bird is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as we found.' It introduces a comparison from one case to a similar one.
Makes it fit (here, permitted to eat).
'So too.' The second half of the comparison.
'From the hands of,' meaning from (out of the state of).

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר builds his proof in two stages: first a קל וחומר (animal to bird, for שחיטה), and then a מה מצינו (שחיטה to מליקה).

phrases.english: Just as we found with its slaughter –
that it renders it fit for eating,
and purifies it, even when it is a tereifa, from its impurity;
so too its pinching,
which renders it fit for eating –
phrases.notes: מליקה is what makes a bird offering permitted to eat, just as שחיטה does for a regular bird.

phrases.english: should purify it, even when it is a tereifa, from its impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the result of the קל וחומר and carries it over to מליקה.
steps.raayaObject: That מליקה keeps a bird offering that is a טריפה from טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to שחיטה, since both acts make the bird fit to eat.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the proof only goes as far as the animal, so slaughter helps but pinching does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי uses the rule of דיו to limit the derivation: the bird is treated only like an animal, and for an animal only שחיטה protects, not מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: it is enough for it to be like the carcass of an animal. Its slaughter purifies it, but its pinching does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי accepts רבי מאיר's first step about שחיטה, but he rejects the second step that moves the rule to מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of דיו says that something learned through a קל וחומר cannot go further than its source. Since the whole idea came from an animal, and an animal is protected only by שחיטה (מליקה does not exist for animals), the bird is protected only by שחיטה too. So a pinched bird that is a טריפה still makes the eater טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough for it.' This is the rule of דַּיּוֹ: a קל וחומר cannot teach more than its source has.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: What is learned from a קל וחומר is only like the case it was learned from.

steps.whatToRemember: All three תנאים agree that a נבלת עוף makes the eater טמא. רבי מאיר says both שחיטה and מליקה protect a bird that turns out to be a טריפה. רבי יוסי (through דיו) says only שחיטה protects, not מליקה. רבי יהודה says the pinched טריפה bird is טמא, and the גמרא later (steps 10-11) shows that for him even a slaughtered טריפה bird is טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not rejecting the whole קל וחומר. He agrees that שחיטה protects a bird that is a טריפה. He only refuses to stretch the rule to מליקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear example of how the rule of דיו limits a קל וחומר: the conclusion can never be stronger than the source case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
it is enough for it to be like the carcass of an animal –
phrases.notes: A rule learned from an animal can't give the bird more than the animal itself has.

phrases.english: its slaughter purifies it,
but not its pinching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: דַּיָּהּ כְּנִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second stage of רבי מאיר's proof (from שחיטה to מליקה) and keeps the first stage.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the move from שחיטה to מליקה. The קל וחומר for שחיטה itself stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule learned from an animal cannot go beyond the animal (דיו), and for an animal only שחיטה protects.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really ignore the rule of דיו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר: how can he ignore דיו when דיו is a Torah rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does רבי מאיר really not use the rule of "דיו"? But "דיו" is a rule from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised at רבי מאיר. In the משנה, he did not seem to accept the rule of דיו, and the גמרא asks how that is possible if דיו comes from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רבי יוסי limited the קל וחומר with דיו: the bird can only be as protected as an animal, so only שחיטה works, not מליקה. רבי מאיר seems to ignore that limit. If דיו is a Torah law, every תנא should have to follow it, so רבי מאיר's position looks impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is enough." The rule that what you learn from a קל וחומר cannot be stricter than its source.
Does not expound, meaning he does not use or apply this rule.
From the Torah itself, not a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: Gemara:
And does Rabbi Meir not expound the rule of "it is enough"?!
phrases.notes: This is about the משנה, where רבי יוסי answered רבי מאיר with דיו and רבי מאיר seemed to ignore it.

phrases.english: But "it is enough" is from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רבי מאיר could have rejected רבי יוסי's דיו argument from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's position, which seems to ignore דיו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דיו is a Torah rule. So no תנא should be allowed to reject it, but רבי מאיר seems to.

steps.title: The proof that דיו comes from the Torah: מרים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses the story of מרים to show that דיו is built into the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: How does a קל וחומר work? The Torah says, "And ה׳ said to משה: If her father had spit in her face, etc." By קל וחומר, being rebuked by the שכינה should mean fourteen days. Instead we say: it is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its question. It shows that the Torah itself uses the rule of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After her father's rebuke, a girl would hide in shame seven days. Logic says a rebuke from the שכינה should be stricter, maybe fourteen days. But the Torah gives מרים only seven days. That shows the result of a קל וחומר is capped at the level of its source, which is דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: By the reasoning of a קל וחומר: if something is true in a lighter case, it is surely true in a stricter case.
"Spit, he would spit." Here it means a father's rebuke of his daughter.
The Divine Presence, meaning ה׳.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for what comes from the reasoning to be like the case it was learned from.

phrases.english: As it was taught: How does the reasoning of a kal vachomer work?
"And ה׳ said to Moshe:
If her father had but spit in her face, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:14. The rest of the פסוק says she would be ashamed seven days, so מרים is closed out of the camp seven days.

phrases.aramaic: קַל וְחוֹמֶר לַשְּׁכִינָה אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם;
phrases.english: by kal vachomer, for a rebuke from the Divine Presence, it should be fourteen days;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן.
phrases.english: rather, it is enough for what comes from the reasoning to be like its source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 5 that דיו is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That דיו is a Torah rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the story of מרים in במדבר 12:14.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for the rule of דיו. It shows up in many places in ש״ס.

steps.title: רבי מאיר is learning from a פסוק, not a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין explains that רבי מאיר is reading a פסוק, so דיו does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: רבי מאיר found a פסוק and is expounding it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי מאיר does accept דיו, but his ruling does not come from a קל וחומר at all; it comes from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דיו only limits a קל וחומר. If רבי מאיר's ruling comes straight from a פסוק, there is nothing for דיו to cap. So the קל וחומר in the משנה was not his real source, and the next lines will show which פסוק he uses.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse in the Torah.
He found.
He is expounding, learning a law from the wording of a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Avin, said:
Rabbi Meir found a verse and is expounding it –

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי אָבִין: רַבִּי מֵאִיר קְרָא אַשְׁכַּח וְקָדָרֵשׁ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the source of the ruling: it comes from a פסוק, not from a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי מאיר's ruling rested on a קל וחומר, so it would have to be limited by דיו.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר learns his ruling from a פסוק, so דיו does not apply.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not rejecting דיו. He agrees it is a Torah rule. He just isn't using a קל וחומר here.

steps.title: The פסוק that pairs animal and bird, and the question it raises
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes "זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף" and asks where a בהמה and an עוף could ever share a law, since their טומאה rules look opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: "This is the law of the animal and the bird." But in which law are an animal and a bird the same? An animal makes things טמא by touching and by carrying, but a bird does not make things טמא by touching or carrying! A bird makes clothes טמא when it is in the throat, but an animal does not make clothes טמא when it is in the throat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי מאיר's פסוק and starts to explain it. It asks a question to show that the פסוק must be teaching something new. This is setup: the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts בהמה and עוף together as one "תורה". But their נבלה laws are reversed. A בהמה is מטמא by touching and carrying but not in the throat, and an עוף is the opposite. Since they share no טומאה rule, the פסוק must be pointing to some other law where they are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the animal and the bird. The פסוק treats them as one group.
Touching. One way a נבלה passes on טומאה.
Carrying. Another way a נבלה passes on טומאה.
The throat, the place of swallowing.
Makes clothes טמא.

phrases.english: "This is the law of the animal and of the bird" –
but in which law
is an animal equal to a bird and a bird to an animal?
An animal makes things impure by touching and by carrying,
a bird does not make things impure by touching or by carrying!
A bird makes clothing impure while it is in the throat,

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה!
phrases.english: an animal does not make clothing impure while it is in the throat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בְּאֵיזוֹ תּוֹרָה שָׁוְותָה בְּהֵמָה לְעוֹף וְעוֹף לִבְהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the פסוק that step 7 said רבי מאיר is expounding, and starts to explain it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ruling that מליקה protects a טריפה bird from נבלה טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question shows the פסוק cannot be about ordinary טומאה rules. That makes room for רבי מאיר's reading, which comes next.

steps.title: What makes a bird fit to eat also removes its טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. The comparison of בהמה and עוף teaches that whatever makes each one fit to eat also stops a טְרֵפָה from being טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק comes to tell you this. With an animal, the thing that makes it fit to eat also saves a טְרֵפָה animal from being טמא. So too with a bird: the thing that makes it fit to eat also saves a טְרֵפָה bird from being טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: In Step 8 the גמרא asked where a בהמה and an עוף could ever share a law. Here it gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal, שחיטה makes it fit to eat, and שחיטה also stops a טְרֵפָה animal from being טמא. The פסוק puts birds in the same group. So whatever makes a bird fit to eat (שחיטה for a regular bird, מליקה for a bird קרבן) also stops a טְרֵפָה bird from being טמא. This is the source for רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal injury or defect, so it is not allowed to be eaten
Makes it fit to be eaten
Makes טָהוֹר; here it means it stops the טומאה from happening

steps.whatToRemember: Whatever makes a creature fit to eat (שחיטה, or מליקה for a bird קרבן) also keeps a טְרֵפָה from being טמא. This works for animals and birds alike.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:
phrases.notes: This answers the question from Step 8: where could an animal and a bird ever share a law?

phrases.english: just as with an animal —
the thing that makes it fit for eating
phrases.notes: For an animal, that means שחיטה.

phrases.english: keeps it from being טמא even when it is a טְרֵפָה;
so too a bird —
the thing that makes it fit for eating
phrases.notes: For a bird this can be שחיטה, or מליקה when the bird is a קרבן.

phrases.english: keeps it from being טמא even when it is a טְרֵפָה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 8 about where a בהמה and an עוף share a law.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They share this law: whatever makes each one fit to eat also stops a טְרֵפָה from being טמא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that מליקה stops a טְרֵפָה bird from being טמא

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks for the reasoning of רבי יהודה, who holds that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה bird still makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the מחלוקת and asks where רבי יהודה gets his view. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's source is now in place. רבי יהודה holds that even after שחיטה, a טְרֵפָה bird is still טמא. So the גמרא wants to know his source in the פסוקים too.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And what is the reason of רבי יהודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי מאיר's source, the גמרא asks for the source of the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the Torah רבי יהודה learns that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה bird still makes things טמא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns from the extra word טְרֵפָה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה points out that the word טְרֵפָה in the פסוק seems extra. He says it must be there to include a טְרֵפָה that was slaughtered, which still makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He found a פסוק and read a lesson from it: "נבלה טרפה". רבי יהודה said: Why does the פסוק mention טְרֵפָה? If it means a טְרֵפָה that is still alive, that can't be, because the פסוק says נְבֵלָה (a dead animal). If it means a טְרֵפָה that died by itself, it is already counted as a נְבֵלָה. So the word must come to include a טְרֵפָה that someone slaughtered: it still makes things טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבי יהודה's source: an extra word in the פסוק about eating a bird נְבֵלָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה checks every possible meaning of "טְרֵפָה". A live טְרֵפָה can't make things טמא, because the פסוק is talking about a dead creature. A טְרֵפָה that died by itself is already a נְבֵלָה. The only case left is a טְרֵפָה that was slaughtered, so the Torah is teaching that it stays טמא even after שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature that died without a proper שחיטה
He found a פסוק and taught a lesson from it
To include (one more case)
It makes things טמא

phrases.english: He found a verse and taught from it:
"A carcass, a טְרֵפָה".

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: טְרֵפָה לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרָה?
phrases.english: רבי יהודה said: Why was טְרֵפָה mentioned?
If it means a live טְרֵפָה —
but "carcass" is what is stated!
If it means a טְרֵפָה that is not alive —
it is already included in "carcass"!
Rather, it comes to include a טְרֵפָה that was slaughtered,
that it makes things טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 by giving רבי יהודה's source in the פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word טְרֵפָה in ויקרא 17:15 would be extra unless it means a slaughtered טְרֵפָה, so a slaughtered טְרֵפָה bird is still טמא.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: the same reading of the fat פסוק leads to an impossible result
steps.stepSummary: רב שֵׁיזְבִי reads the פסוק about the fat of a נְבֵלָה and a טְרֵפָה the same way רבי יהודה read his פסוק. That reading would show that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה's meat is טמא, and that can't be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שֵׁיזְבִי said to him: If so, look at the פסוק "the fat of a carcass and the fat of a טְרֵפָה". There too we should say: if it means a live טְרֵפָה, "carcass" is already stated. If it means a טְרֵפָה that is not alive, it is already included in "carcass". So it must come to include a slaughtered טְרֵפָה, and teach that its fat is טָהוֹר. Does that mean its meat does make things טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שֵׁיזְבִי attacks רבי יהודה's method. He uses the very same reasoning on a different פסוק and shows that it leads to a bad conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat פסוק also mentions both נְבֵלָה and טְרֵפָה. By רבי יהודה's method, the extra word must mean a slaughtered טְרֵפָה whose fat is טָהוֹר. If the Torah needed to say that the fat is טָהוֹר, the meat would have to be טמא. But this פסוק is about animals, and for an animal שחיטה does stop a טְרֵפָה from being טמא (as Steps 4 and 9 said). So the reasoning proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge that pushes an argument too far)
The forbidden fats of an animal
By implication; from this we would learn

steps.confusionAlert: רב שֵׁיזְבִי is not saying the fat פסוק teaches anything new about טומאה. He is showing that רבי יהודה's way of reading the extra word, if used on the fat פסוק, would give a result about animals that nobody accepts.

phrases.english: רב שֵׁיזְבִי said to him:
If that is so,
for it is written: "And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a טְרֵפָה" —
there too, let us say:
If it means a live טְרֵפָה —
"carcass" is already stated,
if it means a טְרֵפָה that is not alive —
it is already included in "carcass"!
Rather, it comes to include a טְרֵפָה that was slaughtered,
that its fat is טָהוֹר.
Does that imply that it does make things טמא?
phrases.notes: "It" here means the meat of that slaughtered טְרֵפָה animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁיזְבִי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method רבי יהודה used in Step 11 by applying it to a parallel פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי יהודה reads the extra word טְרֵפָה in Step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading of ויקרא 7:24 would mean that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה animal's meat is טמא. That goes against the accepted rule that שחיטה stops a טְרֵפָה animal from being טמא, so the method proves too much.

steps.title: A source shows a slaughtered טְרֵפָה animal is not טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רב שֵׁיזְבִי's challenge with a teaching from רב, also taught in a ברייתא. It learns from the פסוק that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה animal does not make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב, and some say a ברייתא taught: "And if some of the animal dies" means that some animals make things טמא and some do not. Which one does not? A טְרֵפָה that was slaughtered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a clear source to prove that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה animal is not טמא. This makes רב שֵׁיזְבִי's challenge from Step 12 even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, reading the fat פסוק the way רבי יהודה reads his פסוק would make a slaughtered טְרֵפָה's meat טמא. This source shows that cannot be right, because a slaughtered טְרֵפָה does not make things טמא at all. So the word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק must have some other job.

keyTerms.meaning: Some of / part of
Makes things טמא
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
"And if some of the animals dies"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39. The word מִן, "some of," is what the teaching is built on.

phrases.english: some animals make things impure,
and some animals do not make things impure.
And which one is that?
That is a tereifa that someone slaughtered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב שֵׁיזְבִי's challenge by proving that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה is not טמא.
steps.raayaObject: That a slaughtered טְרֵפָה animal does not make things טמא, so the extra-word reading in Step 12 cannot be right.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב (or a ברייתא) on ויקרא 11:39, "וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה".

steps.title: The word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק leaves out a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק is not extra. It is needed to leave out a non-kosher animal, because the rule of טְרֵפָה only applies to kinds of animals that can be kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the word טְרֵפָה is needed to leave out a non-kosher animal. It teaches that the rule is only for an animal whose kind can become a טְרֵפָה. A non-kosher animal is left out, because its kind has no טְרֵפָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge to רבי יהודה continues. Since the word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק cannot mean a slaughtered טְרֵפָה (step 13), the גמרא gives it a different job: leaving out a non-kosher animal. This sets up the next step, which turns the same idea against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal is forbidden anyway, so being a טְרֵפָה means nothing for it. The word טְרֵפָה tells us the fat rule only covers kosher kinds of animals. A non-kosher animal is left out of that rule, so its fat stays טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (for another teaching)
To leave out / exclude
Here: a non-kosher animal
In its kind / species

steps.confusionAlert: Here טְמֵאָה does not mean "impure." It means a non-kosher kind of animal.

phrases.english: Rather, the word "tereifa" is needed
phrases.notes: He means the word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק, ויקרא 7:24.

phrases.english: to leave out a non-kosher animal;
the rule is for one whose kind can become a tereifa,
which leaves out this one, whose kind has no tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in Steps 12-13 about what the word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק teaches, by giving it its own job. This builds toward the challenge to רבי יהודה in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the word: it is not extra, it teaches something else.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word טְרֵפָה in the fat פסוק looks extra, so it might teach something about a slaughtered טְרֵפָה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word teaches that only kosher kinds are included, which leaves out a non-kosher animal.

steps.title: Then the bird פסוק should also just leave out a non-kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: Using the same idea, the גמרא challenges רבי יהודה. Maybe the word טְרֵפָה in the bird פסוק also just leaves out a non-kosher bird, so it is not a source for his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, say the word טְרֵפָה leaves out a non-kosher bird, whose kind has no טְרֵפָה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from Step 14 back against רבי יהודה. If the word works that way in the fat פסוק, it could work that way in the bird פסוק too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, רבי יהודה said the word טְרֵפָה in the bird פסוק was extra, so it must include a slaughtered טְרֵפָה. Now the גמרא says the word may have a normal job: leaving out a non-kosher bird. If so, רבי יהודה has lost his source.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
A non-kosher bird

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the bird פסוק that רבי יהודה used back in Step 11.

phrases.english: say it leaves out a non-kosher bird,
whose kind has no tereifa!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of Step 14 to the bird פסוק, which challenges רבי יהודה's source from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim in Step 11 that the word טְרֵפָה in the bird פסוק is extra.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word טְרֵפָה leaves out a non-kosher animal in the fat פסוק, it can also leave out a non-kosher bird in the bird פסוק. Then it is not extra.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns the non-kosher bird from the word נְבֵלָה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה already learns about the non-kosher bird from the word נְבֵלָה. So the word טְרֵפָה is still extra and free for his teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה learns the rule of a non-kosher bird from the word נְבֵלָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה. He does not need the word טְרֵפָה to leave out a non-kosher bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word נְבֵלָה already teaches that a non-kosher bird's carcass is left out, the word טְרֵפָה has no job there. That means it really is extra, and רבי יהודה can use it to teach that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה bird is טמא. His source from Step 11 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from
A carcass that died without proper שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, the word טְרֵפָה in the bird פסוק stays extra because the non-kosher bird is learned from נְבֵלָה. So he can use it to teach that a slaughtered טְרֵפָה bird makes things טמא.

phrases.english: A non-kosher bird, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
he learns from the word "neveila."

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹף טָמֵא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִנְּבֵילָה נָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 and keeps רבי יהודה's source from Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: the exclusion comes from another word, so the word in question stays extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word טְרֵפָה in the bird פסוק is needed to leave out a non-kosher bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה learns that from נְבֵלָה, so the word טְרֵפָה is free to include a slaughtered טְרֵפָה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה learns the non-kosher bird from the word נְבֵלָה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה learning from the word נְבֵלָה that the carcass of a non-kosher bird does not make garments טמא in the throat. This proves the answer of Step 16.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, you might think the carcass of a non-kosher bird makes a person's clothing טמא when it is in his throat. So the פסוק says, 'A נְבֵלָה or a טְרֵפָה he shall not eat.' This טומאה applies only to a bird that is forbidden because of 'do not eat a נְבֵלָה.' That leaves out this bird. It is not forbidden because of 'do not eat a נְבֵלָה.' It is forbidden because of 'do not eat a non-kosher animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its last answer. The ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה really does learn about the non-kosher bird from the word נְבֵלָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16 the גמרא claimed that רבי יהודה leaves out the non-kosher bird using the word נְבֵלָה, not the word טְרֵפָה. This ברייתא proves that claim. The word נְבֵלָה only covers a bird whose ban comes from the נְבֵלָה prohibition, and a non-kosher bird is already banned for a different reason, so it is left out. That means the word טְרֵפָה is still extra, and רבי יהודה can use it for his own teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a non-kosher bird
The throat, the place of swallowing
The פסוק teaches us (to say otherwise)
The prohibition of eating an animal that died without proper שחיטה
The prohibition of eating a non-kosher kind of animal

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the word נְבֵלָה leaves out the non-kosher bird, because that bird is forbidden as a non-kosher kind and not as a נְבֵלָה. So the word טְרֵפָה is still extra, and it can be the source for his teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two different bans. A non-kosher bird is forbidden because of what kind of bird it is (טָמֵא). A נְבֵלָה is a kosher kind that is forbidden because it died without שחיטה. The ברייתא's whole point depends on keeping these two apart.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One might think that the carcass of a non-kosher bird
makes garments impure when it is in the throat?
The verse says: "A carcass or a tereifa he shall not eat"

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאִיסּוּרוֹ מִשּׁוּם בַּל תֹּאכַל נְבֵילָה
phrases.english: meaning one that is forbidden because of 'do not eat a carcass'
This one is left out, since it is not forbidden
because of 'do not eat a carcass'
but because of 'do not eat a non-kosher animal.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a ברייתא as proof for the תירוץ in Step 16, that רבי יהודה learns the non-kosher bird exclusion from the word נְבֵלָה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהודה excludes the non-kosher bird using the word נְבֵלָה, which leaves the word טְרֵפָה extra.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה reading the פסוק נְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה לֹא יֹאכַל (ויקרא 22:8).
